correctness.rationale: For 0<q<=(-2+sqrt(6))/2 and 2q³+4q²<=t<(1-q²)/(2-q²), n=3 of Kahler–Obermaier Theorem 2.1 is exactly the lower bound, the n>=4 inequalities are q²+2q<=1/2, and the strict initial inequality is the upper bound; all Jacobi coefficients lie in (0,1). At x=0, the recurrence forces odd P_n=0 and computes even values and Haar weights exactly: h(2m)P_2m(0)²=ρ q^{2m²-m}/(q;q)_{2m}, ρ=t(1-q)/(q(1-t)). Supergeometric summability gives an actual l² Jacobi eigenvector, so the zero atom equals [1+ρ sum_{m>=1} q^{2m²-m}/(q;q)_{2m}]^-1. Even-part extraction from Euler q-binomial identity evaluates that sum as (prod_{j>=0}(1-q^{2j+1}))^-1-1. For t=q, ρ=1; derivative dρ/dt>0 proves strict mass decrease. Finite exact rational tests of recurrence/normalization supplement, but do not replace, spectral and infinite-series reasoning.
